paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the servant prayed, and then he paid attention. He asked the LORD for a sign, and he stayed alert for the answer. Even while Rebekah was watering those camels, he "watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success" (Genesis 24:21). He didn't pray and then wander off to check his phone.

Notice the timing, friend. Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah was already coming out with her jar (Genesis 24:15). He gave her gifts and asked about her family and a place to stay, and once she answered, he bowed down and worshiped (Genesis 24:22-26). Then he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master" (Genesis 24:27), and I'm LOUD about this one: that thank you is a habit worth baking into every day.

So here's what I want you to take to your own oven, baker. You can bring the LORD your real, specific needs, and you can expect to see Him at work. When He answers, don't just grab the answer and run. Stop and say thank you, because a servant who prayed, watched and worshiped is a good teacher for all of us.
